question: Should approval-triggered apply, reject, and quarantine actions be permanently bound to the proposal version described in the prompt, while direct service, CLI, and tool calls remain proposal-ID compatible?
rationale: This changes the operator-facing lifecycle contract deliberately: stale prompt decisions fail instead of acting on revised content. Tests can prove implementation mechanics but cannot choose that permanent product and compatibility policy.

options.title: Approve snapshot binding
options.body: Adopt the PR's fail-closed approval semantics while preserving optional version checks for direct callers.

options.title: Preview without binding
options.body: Keep exact previews but remove automatic proposal-version injection from lifecycle approval execution.

options.title: Defer the core feature
options.body: Retain summary-only approvals until maintainers sponsor a different proposal-review contract.

recommendation.title: Approve snapshot binding
recommendation.body: Adopt the PR's fail-closed approval semantics while preserving optional version checks for direct callers.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work directly owns the approval resolver and its auto-versus-pending behavior.
